newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-THOME REPLACES JUSTICE ON AL ALL-STAR TEAM.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-THOME REPLACES JUSTICE ON AL ALL-STAR TEAM.

text.p: Jim Thome, the slugging first baseman of the Cleveland Indians, will get to participate in Tuesday's All-Star game after all as he was named to the squad Sunday as a replacement for injured teammate David Justice.

Thome, who will get to play in front of the hometown crowd at Jacobs Field, was among the most prominent players passed over by Yankees manager Joe Torre when the reserves were named last week. He is hitting .298 with 24 homers and 62 RBI.
Thome was involved in the closest race among the All-Star starters, losing the starting nod to New York's Tino Martinez by just over 19,000 votes.

The former third baseman will be taking the place of Justice, who was elected as a starting outfielder. Justice, in his first season in the American League, is suffering from a hyperextended left elbow.
Justice, acquired from the Atlanta Braves along with outfielder Marquis Grissom in a blockbuster deal for Kenny Lofton during spring training, is hitting .335 with 17 homers and 47 RBI.

Justice is the third player to be selected to the AL squad who has decided not to play. Orioles pitcher Jimmy Key has declined to play as he is getting married during the break. Frank Thomas declined in order to rest his sore rib cage.

Saturday, Torre named his own outfielder, Paul O'Neill to replace Thomas. But Thome, who will be making his first All-Star appearance, got the nod this time and will join teammate Sandy Alomar on the squad.
Baltimore's Brady Anderson is questionable for the game after being hit by a pair of pitches on Saturday.

The National League also had a pair of late scratches as San Diego Padres centre fielder Steve Finley and Florida Marlins catcher Charles Johnson were named Sunday as replacements for injured players Kenny Lofton of the Atlanta Braves and Todd Hundley of the New York Mets.
